newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks slide on economic uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks slide on economic uncertainty.

text.p: Colombian stocks continued their downward slide as uncertainty over measures included in the government's recently declared economic emergency package continued to pervade markets.
Bogota's IBB index drifted down 0.28 percent to 955.04 on trade of 884 million pesos -- its 10th consecutive fall.

Medellin's IBOMED index fell 0.78 percent to 14,762.81 on one billion pesos -- its ninth straight drop. In economic emergency measures decreed last week, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo announced that a number of tax loopholes would be closed and the decision to begin considering share earnings as taxable income.

The government decreed a state of economic emergency on Januart 13 to combat a yawning fiscal deficit and stem a heavy influx of dollars into Colombia, which was seen as undermining Colombian exports.
"Investors are still looking at their possibilities in the share market. They're very unhappy with the tax ruling," one Bogota broker said.
The biggest fall in Bogota and Medellin was cigarette maker Coltabaco, which fell 7.14 percent to 3,250. It is now back at similar levels to those at which it opened the year, brokers said.

Banco de Colombia fell 3.33 percent to 435 in Medellin and 0.92 percent to 430 in Bogota. Brewing giant Bavaria, one of the star performers of the year so far, was unchanged in Bogota at 5,550 and edged up 0.73 percent in Medellin.
Banco de Bogota gained in both markets, up 1.72 percent at 5,900 in Medellin and up 0.16 percent at 5,910 in Bogota.
The tiny Cali-based Bolsa de Occidente gained 0.2 percent to close at 127.51 on 216 million peso volume.
